title: Portulan Workspace Definition v1
description: The manifest at the root of a workspace. It is an index, not a container: it names the slots the engine resolves against and points at the Markdown that holds each slot's content and rationale. Written in a deliberately small subset of JSON Schema 2020-12 — see spec/README.md for the subset and for what validates it.

portulan.description: Version block. `spec` is the Workspace Definition version this manifest is written against; the engine uses it to decide whether a migration is needed.

spec.description: Workspace Definition version, MAJOR.MINOR. A MAJOR bump means a migration exists.

workspace.description: Optional version of this workspace's own content, SemVer. Lets a workspace shipped as a plugin be pinned by consumers.

name.description: Stable identifier for this workspace. Lowercase, hyphenated — it is used as a plugin name when the workspace ships through a feed.

summary.description: One line an agent can read before loading anything else.

kind.description: Which of the three workspace kinds this is. The distinction is load-bearing: a demo workspace is written to be read by strangers and must carry no real internal policy, while a repository or portfolio workspace carries exactly that.

slots.description: Path slots. Every value resolves to a file or a directory relative to the workspace root. Fragments are not permitted: a slot addressed by `#anchor` cannot be checked, so a slot's content must be a whole file. The pattern alone cannot say WHICH slot may leave the workspace directory — `constitution` is the only one expected to, and spec/slots.md has `doctor` report (never fail) any other slot that does.

identity.description: Who this team is, the stack, and the glossary. The first thing an agent reads after the kernel.

principles.description: The team's own binding principles — the constitution slot. What makes an agent work THIS team's way rather than generically.

constitution.description: Optional. A separate document this team's work is graded against, when one exists apart from `principles`. This is the slot permitted to point outside the workspace directory, because a product's constitution usually lives with the product rather than with the workspace.

gates.description: The gate map: this team's concrete actions bound to the engine's Auto / Propose / Gated tiers, plus the triage threshold.

dod.description: Optional. The workspace's extension of core's definition-of-done floor. Absent means core's floor stands alone, which is valid.

memory.description: Optional. Directory of durable facts, one per file, each carrying provenance.

repos.description: Optional. Directory of repo cards, one per repository this workspace covers.

handoffs.description: Optional. Directory of dated handoffs, filenames leading with an ISO date.

proposals.description: Optional. Directory of agent-drafted rule changes awaiting the human gate.

verify.description: The executable half of done. A workspace declares its recipes and names the default; a repo card may override it and a task may specialize it.

default.description: The `id` of the recipe the Stop-gate runs when nothing more specific applies.

products.description: The product layer, repeated. A workspace may cover many products — a portfolio workspace covers all of a studio's — so mission/what/why and agent affordances belong to a product, not to the workspace. A workspace with one product still lists one.

affordances.description: Optional workspace-level default for agent affordances, inherited by any product that does not declare its own. The same more-specific-wins rule as the resolution cascade, applied inside the workspace.

packs.description: Optional. The packs this workspace composes, in cascade order — core < pack < workspace. Named here so a workspace can state which stack, tool, and ritual layers it depends on rather than leaving it to be inferred.

path.description: A relative path to a file or directory, resolved from the workspace root. The leading character may not be `/` (no absolute paths) and `:` is excluded (no URLs), so `../` is the only way out of the workspace — which is deliberate, since escaping should be visible in the value itself.

filePath.description: A relative path to a file — same rules as `path`, and must not end in `/`.

dirPath.description: A relative path to a directory — same rules as `path`, and must end in `/`, so the intent is legible without touching the filesystem.

recipe.description: One verify recipe: what to run, and what it needs in order to run at all.

run.description: The command, as it would be typed from the repository root.

requires.description: The tools the recipe needs. Declared rather than discovered, because a recipe that cannot run must be distinguishable from one that ran and failed — the difference between exit 2 and exit 1.

doc.description: Where the recipe's checks and their known limits are written up. Resolved from the WORKSPACE root, like every other path in this manifest — unlike the sibling `run`, which is a command line and is therefore written as it would be typed from the repository root. The two bases differ because the two fields are read by different things: `doc` by something resolving paths, `run` by a shell.

name.description: Display name, when it differs from the id.

product.description: The product layer: mission, what it is, why it exists.

affordances.description: What this product offers an agent working on it — entry points, commands, machine-readable contracts, and the honest gaps. Overrides the workspace-level default.

repos.description: The `repos/` card names this product ships from.

provenance.description: How a rule links to the incident that created it. NOT a manifest key — rules live in Markdown records (memory entries, proposals), and this is the normative shape their `provenance:` field is parsed into. One definition, two carriers. Adopted 2026-07-25 from .portulan/proposals/0002-sealed-provenance.md; see spec/slots.md for the reasoning and the honest limits.

oneOf.description: Public — a resolvable link to the incident: a ticket, a PR, a postmortem, a commit.

Sealed — an owner and a date plus the de-identified failure shape, for an incident that cannot leave its owner's layer. The full chain stays in the owner's workspace; what travels is the stamp and the mechanism, never the episode.

owner.description: Who can still see the incident and therefore re-validate the rule.

date.description: ISO date of the incident, which is what the librarian nags against.

shape.description: The de-identified failure: the inputs, the wrong outcome, and why the obvious guard misses it. The bar is that someone who never saw the incident can still write the rule's test.
